rows.note: Package `prose-sanitiser`. It provides the twelve CLIs that agentbox puts on `PATH` (`agentbox:flake.nix:1835-1839`) and re-exports the lower crates that the server imports (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:32-39`). `audit-website` checks each hop, resolves only to public addresses and pins the connection with `PinnedResolver`. It follows at most 5 redirects and caps bodies at 4 MiB and sitemaps at 64 MiB (`audit/website/mod.rs:21,30,33,256-263,291`). `rewrite-text` accepts only loopback endpoints by default (`rewrite/mod.rs:32,125-133`) and follows no redirects, so the bearer key is never forwarded (`backends.rs:29`). The IPv6 filter has gaps (COV-A-F8).

Reached through `clean-image`, `inspect-image`, `clean-file` and `inspect-file`, and through the server's `/inspect` and `/clean` (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:35-37`). Container and image provenance stripping runs in-process with `img-parts`, `lopdf`, `zip`, `quick-xml` and read-only `c2pa` (`crates/media/Cargo.toml:28-52`). Reads are size-capped. Writes go to a temporary file and are renamed into place, and symlinks are refused (`io.rs:205-222`). The zip budget is enforced on bytes actually produced, not on declared sizes (`ooxml/mod.rs:178-199`). Every `run_capture` call site is in `image/harness.rs`, `image/tools.rs` or `cli/src/rewrite/markllm.rs:122`, so subprocesses run only for the torch and MarkLLM harnesses and the `external-verify` cross-check. Each runs under rlimits, a 64 MiB output cap and a guard against filenames that start with `-`. `rsa` RUSTSEC-2023-0071 is ignored in `deny.toml:19`, with the reason given at `crates/media/Cargo.toml:46-51`. The lockfile resolves `quick-xml` 0.41.0 (`Cargo.lock:2583-2584`). Harness scripts can be loaded from the current directory (COV-A-F5).

Reached through `slop`, which depends on it (`crates/slop/Cargo.toml:15`), and through the CLI's `uk` module (`crates/cli/src/lib.rs:26`). It checks UK English spelling, taking each word's sense into account, against a table generated at build time from vendored VarCon (`build.rs:155-156` reads `data/varcon.txt`). Only spellings that are unambiguous regardless of sense are ever auto-fixed, and only behind `Config::write` (`lib.rs:50-55`). At run time it does no I/O: grep over `crates/uk/src` finds no `std::fs`, `std::process` or `std::net`.

Every other crate depends on it (for example `crates/slop/Cargo.toml:14` and `crates/unicode/Cargo.toml:14`). It defines the shared types: `Finding`, `Severity`, `ConfidenceTier` and `Patch`, the `Check` and `Fix` traits, SARIF and JSONL reports, and suppressions. Grep finds no filesystem, process or network use. It does read environment variables (`env_usize`, `env_nonempty`, `lib.rs:125-134`), which the "no I/O" claim at `lib.rs:1` does not mention. That omission is immaterial.

Reached through `clean-text` and `inspect-text`, through `media`, which depends on it (`crates/media/Cargo.toml:25`), and through the server's text path (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:39`). This is Layer A. It classifies invisible and format-class code points and decodes hidden payloads carried in variation selectors, tag characters and zero-width characters. It also detects homoglyphs with UTS #39 through `unicode-security` 0.1.2. Its bidi policy depends on context, and it closes a fullwidth-folding gap in `unicode-security` (`confusables.rs:29-40`). Grep finds no I/O.

Reached through `slop-scan` (`crates/cli/src/bin/slop_scan.rs:28,168`), through `slop-detect`, and through the server's `/rules` (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:38`). It holds the prose scanner for AI writing tells and the design anti-pattern scanner. Both only report, and no rule supplies a fix. The crate walks directories and reads files itself, although the workspace manifest says it does not (COV-A-F3). An unreadable file counts as scanned with zero findings (COV-A-F4).

An unpublished axum service (`publish = false`). It binds `127.0.0.1:8765` by default and the bearer key is optional. A body limit applies, and client filenames are cut to their basename inside a per-request temporary directory. Agentbox bakes the binary but nothing starts it. Grep finds only the derivation comment and a skill reference (`agentbox:skills/prose-sanitiser/references/provenance.md:306`). `/clean` can start the torch harness (COV-A-F7).

The crate root, which every binary imports. It holds the XML DOM over `quick-xml` 0.41.0, the entity tables, `pyfmt` (formatting that matches the earlier Python output) and `semantic_review`. `semantic_review` is library-only: no `[[bin]]` uses it, as a grep over `src/bin` confirms. It does no I/O itself and builds System One `POST /v1/systemone` request bodies for a transport the caller supplies (`semantic_review.rs:14-17,29-36`). It is absent from the shipped `v0.1.0` (COV-A-F1). The trust-boundary claim at `lib.rs:4-7` promises more than the code does (COV-A-F2).

Reached only through `mermaid-extract`, which the diagram-design and mermaid-diagrams skills call (`agentbox:skills/diagram-design/SKILL.md:518`; `agentbox:skills/mermaid-diagrams/SKILL.md:120`). It lexes and parses flowchart, sequence, state and ER diagrams into the normalised IR. Source is read through a bounded `take` and capped at 4 MiB, with at most 2,000 nodes and 5,000 edges. Nothing here evaluates or renders its input.

Reached only through `drawio-extract` (`src/bin/drawio_extract.rs:17-19,66-67`). It decodes raw XML, base64-encoded raw deflate, and diagrams embedded in PNG `tEXt`/`zTXt`/`iTXt` chunks or an SVG `content` attribute, then flattens `mxGraphModel` into the IR. DTD and entity declarations are rejected. Each decompression is capped at 64 MiB, but there is no node or edge cap and no total across pages (COV-A-F2).

Reached through `diagram-self-check` (`src/bin/self_check.rs:16-17,37`), which the diagram-design skill's checklist requires (`agentbox:skills/diagram-design/SKILL.md:471`). It checks the accessible-SVG contract, single-file safety (no remote assets other than Google Fonts, no event-handler attributes, no script except the canonical motion controller) and the motion contract. The bundled template is byte-identical to agentbox's skill copy (both SHA-256 `d6953d2f…`). If `/opt/agentbox/...` is absent, the template can be loaded from the current directory (COV-A-F6).

The three binaries agentbox bakes (`agentbox:lib/diagram-ir.nix:9-17`) and the diagram-design skill calls (`agentbox:skills/diagram-design/SKILL.md:471,518`). `drawio-extract` checks the file size from its metadata, then reads the whole file with `fs::read` (`drawio_extract.rs:52-65`), so a file that grows between the two steps escapes the cap. `diagram-self-check` reads each file with no size cap (`self_check.rs:42`). Both are local CLIs that run on files the operator chooses.
Cargo integration tests and golden fixtures (`tests/*.rs`, `tests/fixtures/`, `tests/golden/`). Neither the library nor the binaries import them, and they have no product role.

findings.finding_and_consequence: Agentbox builds diagram-ir `v0.1.0` (`16b1f84`). The audited pin `15cba16` adds `src/semantic_review.rs` (865 lines) and a rustfmt-only change to `xmldom.rs`. The vendored lockfile is byte-identical to the lockfile at both revisions. Consequence: the audited code is not the code users run, and DI-01-S1-01 (the Jev option) is unavailable inside agentbox until the tag moves.

The crate claims "hard caps on … node count and edge count", but only the Mermaid path has them. On the draw.io path each `<diagram>` page can inflate to 64 MiB, the page loop keeps no running total, and every parsed page is held in memory. Consequence: memory is bounded only by the number of pages times 64 MiB, plus the parsed page data. By that bound, from the code and not measured, a 32 MiB input of highly compressed pages could reach GiB. The exposure is the diagram-design skill importing a `.drawio` file someone else supplied.

The workspace manifest says `slop` is "pure Rust with no filesystem access", but `slop` walks directories and reads files itself. It reads with plain `std::fs::read`, not the capped `read_capped` in `media/src/io.rs:165`. Consequence: code that embeds the published `prose-sanitiser-slop` crate gets filesystem access its documentation rules out, and a large file in a scanned tree is read whole into memory.

Both binaries reject a path that does not exist. A path that exists but cannot be read, or an unreadable file inside a scanned tree, reaches `scan_file`, which returns no findings, and `slop-scan` still counts it in `files_scanned`. Consequence: a permission error or a broken link inside the tree reads as a clean pass. The comment at `slop_detect.rs:62-64` calls that outcome "the worst possible answer" for a CI gate.

If `PROSE_SANITISER_SCRIPTS_DIR` is unset and `/opt/agentbox/skills/prose-sanitiser` is absent, `scripts_dir()` falls back to `skills/prose-sanitiser` relative to the current directory. Each harness script, such as `markdiffusion_harness.py`, is then loaded from there and run with the system `python3`. MarkDiffusion needs no environment variable before it starts the child process. Consequence: outside agentbox, running `clean-image --remove-pixel diffusion` inside an untrusted checkout executes that checkout's Python. Inside agentbox the baked path takes precedence.

When `--motion-template` is not passed, `DIAGRAM_DESIGN_SKILL_DIR` is unset and `/opt/agentbox/...` is absent, the self-check loads the canonical motion controller from `./skills/diagram-design/assets/template-motion.html` in preference to the bundled copy. Consequence: a repository can supply both the HTML under check and the "canonical" script it is checked against, which defeats the single-script rule. This applies only outside agentbox.

The bearer key is optional. `/clean` accepts `remove_pixel`, which `clean_image` hands to the CtrlRegen or MarkDiffusion harness, and that harness runs once per request under a 32 GiB address-space cap. The key is compared with a plain string `==`, which does not run in constant time. The default bind is loopback, and agentbox does not run the service. Consequence: if someone binds the service to a network address with no key and the torch harnesses are installed, any client on that network can start torch jobs at will. Without torch installed, each such request still starts a Python child process, which then fails.

The SSRF filter `is_global` unwraps only `::ffff:` IPv4-mapped addresses (`net.rs:146`). It treats NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96`, 6to4 `2002::/16`, Teredo `2001::/32` and IPv4-compatible `::a.b.c.d` addresses as global. Consequence: on a host with a NAT64 or 6to4 gateway, an AAAA record can steer `audit-website` to a private IPv4 service. The comment at `net.rs:139` says the function mirrors Python's `ip_address.is_global`. Whether CPython classifies these ranges the same way cannot be checked from source at the pin, so this finding rests on reachability alone.

The agentbox derivation describes "twelve baked binaries" and "the eleven CLI binaries". The CLI crate declares twelve `[[bin]]` targets and the server adds a thirteenth binary. The agentbox list leaves out the umbrella `sanitise` binary. Consequence: an operator who reads the derivation does not learn that the all-layer pass is on `PATH`.

The route list in the server crate's documentation leaves out `GET /rules`. The media crate's documentation says `c2pa` 0.90, but the manifest pins 0.91 and the lockfile resolves 0.91.7 (`Cargo.lock:458-459`). Consequence: two minor errors in the published rustdoc.

Neither repository has a diagram area, and ES-90 cites only their `Cargo.toml` files. That leaves undescribed, and uncited, the behaviour of sixteen binaries on every agent's `PATH`, an LLM egress path, a website crawler that fetches URLs an attacker can choose, and a subprocess bridge to agentbox's Python harnesses. Consequence: no topic existed that could have caught COV-A-F2 to COV-A-F8, and nothing exists to review a future tag bump against.
